name: Getting started with GGSocial
description: Connect your accounts and plan your first posts.

cards.subject: A brand
says: is one company or project in GGSocial
has its own channels, media, calendar, team and timezone
is the unit that owns a set of channels
cards.use: want the unit that groups one company's channels and team
not: is a single account on one social platform

cards.subject: A channel
says: is one account on one platform
belongs to exactly one brand
is what a post is sent to
cards.use: need the unit that stands for one connected social account
not: is a group of teammates working on a brand

cards.subject: The Composer
says: lets you write base copy once and override it for each channel
shows live character counts as you type
checks per-platform rules while you write
cards.use: want to write one idea for several platforms at once
not: shows every brand on a month grid

cards.subject: The Calendar
says: shows every brand on one month grid
colour-codes posts by brand
lets you drag a post to move it to another day
cards.use: want to see what is planned across your brands this month
not: holds the master rules for each format

cards.subject: The Playbook
says: holds master instructions for each format and kind of engagement
checks limits such as hashtag count and copy length itself
can stop a post from being scheduled when a must rule is broken
cards.use: want to know where the content rules for a brand live
not: lists the posts that failed to publish

cards.subject: Analytics
says: shows what went out and where
reports whatever metrics each platform returns
is where you look back at published posts
cards.use: want to see how published posts performed
not: is where you write the copy for a post

cards.subject: The Publish queue
says: holds anything due on a manual-only channel
gives you copy buttons and media to download
ends with you ticking the item off
cards.use: have a post that you must publish by hand
not: lists every post ever written

cards.subject: The Review inbox
says: collects everything waiting for a person
lets you approve, send back with a note or stop a run
gathers work from the brand's agents in one place
cards.use: want one place to see what is waiting for your decision
not: is where manual posts are copied and pasted

cards.subject: Base copy
says: is the text you write once for all channels
applies to every channel that has no override
is the starting point you tune per platform
cards.use: need the shared text that every channel starts from
not: is the text that only one channel uses

cards.subject: A channel override
says: replaces the base copy on one channel only
lets you tune wording or length to a single platform
leaves the base copy of the other channels untouched
cards.use: need X shorter and Instagram warmer than the shared text
not: changes the base copy on every channel

cards.subject: A live channel
says: is published to by GGSocial itself through the platform's API
needs no one to paste the post at the scheduled time
still goes through the normal approval flow
cards.use: want a post to go out automatically at the scheduled time
not: needs a person to click publish on the platform

cards.subject: A manual-only channel
says: has a platform with no write API for organic content
gets composed, checked, scheduled and queued like any other
ends with a person posting it
cards.use: are on a platform that cannot be published to automatically
not: is skipped by the Composer and Calendar

cards.subject: Copy-ready blocks
says: give a person text prepared to paste into the platform
are prepared for manual-only channels
save retyping when you post by hand
cards.use: post by hand and want the text ready to paste
not: publish the post for you on the platform

cards.subject: Connecting a channel
says: links a social account to a brand
is done by an admin or the owner of the brand
happens before any post can go to that account
cards.use: want to add a new social account to a brand
not: is done by a viewer

cards.subject: Reconnecting a channel
says: restores access after saved permission has lapsed
usually goes through the platform's own sign-in and permission screen
is the usual fix for an expired or failing channel
cards.use: see a channel marked expired
not: requires deleting the whole brand

cards.subject: The connected status
says: shows that GGSocial can currently use the channel
is the healthy state of a channel
cards.use: want to know a channel is ready to use
not: means the channel's saved access has lapsed

cards.subject: The disconnected status
says: shows that no account is currently linked to the channel
tells you the channel needs connecting before it can be used
cards.use: see a channel that has no account linked
not: means the platform rejected the last post

cards.subject: The expired status
says: shows that the channel's saved access has run out
is cleared by reconnecting the account
cards.use: see that a channel's permission has lapsed
not: means the channel was archived

cards.subject: The error status
says: shows that the last attempt to use the channel failed
calls for a look at the channel before more posts are scheduled to it
cards.use: see a channel whose last attempt failed
not: means everything is working normally

cards.subject: A platform API
says: lets software act on an account with the account holder's permission
is what makes automatic publishing possible
is controlled by the platform, not by GGSocial
cards.use: wonder why some platforms can be published to automatically
not: is a setting you switch on in the Composer

cards.subject: The platform permission screen
says: asks you to grant access to your account without sharing your password
is usually shown by the platform itself during connecting
lets you see what access you are granting
cards.use: connect a channel and want to avoid typing your platform password into GGSocial
not: is where you type your GGSocial password

cards.subject: Channel categories
says: group the many platforms GGSocial covers
make channels easier to search and browse
cards.use: want to find a platform among more than a hundred
not: decide which role you have on a brand

cards.subject: Copy buttons
says: put a post's text on your clipboard in one click
sit in the Publish queue next to each item
cards.use: want to paste the post text into a platform quickly
not: publish the post to the platform

cards.subject: The media download
says: gives you the images or video to upload by hand
is offered in the Publish queue
cards.use: need the picture or video for a manual post
not: resizes media for every platform

cards.subject: Platform-specific steps
says: tell you how to finish the post on that platform
differ from one manual-only platform to another
cards.use: are unsure how to post on a particular manual-only platform
not: are identical for every platform

cards.subject: Ticking off a queue item
says: marks the post as published
tells GGSocial that you posted it by hand
is done after the post is live on the platform
cards.use: have just posted a queued item on the platform
not: posts it for you automatically

cards.subject: The awaiting-manual status
says: shows that a post is waiting for a person to publish it
applies to a channel target on a manual-only channel
cards.use: see a target that is waiting for you to post it
not: means the post has already been published

cards.subject: A manual posting checklist
says: has you paste the copy, attach the media and check the preview
ends with ticking the item off in the queue
cards.use: want a routine for posting by hand without mistakes
not: is only needed for live channels

cards.subject: Checking the live post
says: confirms that the post looks right on the platform after you publish by hand
catches missing media or broken links before the audience sees them
cards.use: have published by hand and want to be sure it went out properly
not: is unnecessary once an item is ticked off

cards.subject: A due queue item
says: is a post whose scheduled time has arrived on a manual-only channel
waits for a person rather than going out by itself
cards.use: see a manual item that has reached its scheduled time
not: publishes at the scheduled time on its own

cards.subject: Audience
says: is the group of people a post is written for
shapes the topics, tone and timing of a post
cards.use: want to decide what to say before writing
not: is the list of platforms a brand uses

cards.subject: Tone of voice
says: is how a brand sounds in writing
should stay recognisable across channels
can flex a little between platforms
cards.use: want a brand to sound consistent everywhere
not: is the topic a post is about

cards.subject: A brand voice guide
says: writes down the tone, words to use and words to avoid
helps several writers sound like one brand
cards.use: have more than one person writing for the same brand
not: lists the platform character limits

cards.subject: A hook
says: is the opening line meant to stop the scroll
has to work before the viewer taps to read more
cards.use: want the first words of a post to earn attention
not: is the link at the end of a post

cards.subject: A call to action
says: tells the reader the one thing to do next
is usually one clear request at the end
cards.use: want readers to sign up, reply or click
not: is the opening line of a post

cards.subject: Alt text
says: describes an image for people who cannot see it
helps screen-reader users follow the post
cards.use: add an image and want it to be accessible
not: is a hidden keyword list for search engines

cards.subject: Hashtags
says: label a post with a topic people can follow or search
work best when few and relevant
cards.use: want a post to be found by people interested in a topic
not: are required on every post by every platform

cards.subject: Content pillars
says: are the few recurring themes a brand posts about
stop a feed from feeling random
cards.use: want a steady set of themes to plan around
not: are the colours used on the Calendar

cards.subject: A content mix
says: balances helpful, entertaining and promotional posts
stops a feed from becoming all selling
cards.use: notice that every post is a sales pitch
not: means posting the same text on every channel

cards.subject: Repurposing
says: adapts one idea into formats that suit different platforms
saves effort without pasting identical text everywhere
cards.use: have one good idea and several platforms
not: means reposting identical text everywhere

cards.subject: Evergreen content
says: stays useful long after it is first posted
can be shared again later with a fresh angle
cards.use: want content that does not date quickly
not: is only relevant to a current news event

cards.subject: Posting cadence
says: is how often a brand posts
is better kept steady than burst-and-vanish
cards.use: decide how many posts a week you can keep up
not: is the time of day a post goes out

cards.subject: Plain language
says: uses short, familiar words instead of jargon
makes a post easy to read on a phone
cards.use: want a post anyone can follow at a glance
not: means leaving out the call to action

cards.subject: A campaign
says: groups related posts around one goal and period
lets you judge the posts together
cards.use: are promoting one launch across a few weeks
not: is one post on one channel

cards.subject: The X 280-character limit
says: caps a standard X post at 280 characters
is counted live in the Composer
cards.use: are drafting for X and need to know the length
not: applies to Instagram captions

cards.subject: An X thread
says: splits a long idea into connected posts
is made in GGSocial by separating parts with blank lines
cards.use: have more to say than fits in 280 characters
not: is a single long post that X accepts as is

cards.subject: The Reddit title and subreddit rule
says: needs a title and a subreddit before a post is valid
sends the post to a community, not to a personal feed
cards.use: are preparing a post for Reddit
not: needs only a hashtag

cards.subject: The YouTube title rule
says: needs a title on the video post
is checked in the Composer
cards.use: are preparing a video post for YouTube
not: needs a subreddit
like: The Reddit title and subreddit rule

cards.subject: The Instagram media rule
says: needs an image or video on the post
cannot be satisfied by text alone
cards.use: are preparing a post for Instagram
not: needs a thread

cards.subject: The live character count
says: updates as you type in the Composer
shows how close you are to a platform's limit
cards.use: want to know whether the copy will fit
not: is only shown after you publish

cards.subject: Per-platform rules
says: differ from one platform to another
are checked in the Composer before a post is scheduled
cards.use: wonder why the same text is valid on one channel but not another
not: are the same for every platform

cards.subject: Platform rule changes
says: can alter limits or formats without GGSocial deciding it
are a reason to recheck a channel when a post is rejected
cards.use: find a post that used to work is now rejected
not: never happen once a channel is connected

cards.subject: How emoji count toward a limit
says: can use more than one character of a platform's allowance
are why a post can seem to fit and still be too long
cards.use: are close to a limit and the copy includes emoji
not: never count at all

cards.subject: A draft
says: is a post still being written
has not been sent for approval or scheduled
cards.use: have a post you are still working on
not: is a post waiting for an approver

cards.subject: An absolute instant
says: is one exact moment that does not change with where you are
is how a scheduled time is stored
cards.use: want to know why a scheduled post goes out at one moment for everyone
not: changes depending on each viewer's phone

cards.subject: The brand timezone
says: is the timezone scheduled times are shown in
belongs to the brand, not to each viewer
cards.use: see a scheduled time and wonder which clock it uses
not: is always UTC

cards.subject: Dragging a post on the Calendar
says: moves it to another day
is the quick way to reschedule
cards.use: want to move a planned post to a different day
not: deletes the post and drafts a new one

cards.subject: A posting window
says: is the time range in which a post should go out
can be checked by the Playbook
cards.use: must keep posts inside agreed hours
not: is the length of a video

cards.subject: Testing the best time to post
says: uses your own analytics to see when your audience responds
beats copying a generic best-time chart
cards.use: want to choose posting times for your own audience
not: relies on a single universal best hour

cards.subject: An audience in several timezones
says: means no single hour suits everyone
can be served by posting at more than one hour
cards.use: have followers spread across different countries
not: is solved by posting only at midnight

cards.subject: Batch scheduling
says: plans several posts in one sitting
keeps a feed steady when the team is busy
cards.use: want to plan a week of posts at once
not: publishes everything at the same moment

cards.subject: The needs-approval status
says: shows that a post is waiting for a reviewer
comes after a draft in the normal flow
cards.use: see a post that is waiting for an approver
not: shows that a post is already live

cards.subject: The changes-requested status
says: shows that a reviewer sent the post back for edits
returns the post to its author
cards.use: see a post a reviewer has returned
not: shows that the post was approved

cards.subject: The approved status
says: shows that a reviewer has signed the post off
comes before a post is scheduled
cards.use: see a post that is ready to be scheduled
not: shows that the post is still being written

cards.subject: The scheduled status
says: shows that a post has a time and is waiting to go out
follows approval
cards.use: see a post with a set time that has not gone out yet
not: shows that it was sent back for edits

cards.subject: The publishing status
says: shows that a post is in the middle of going out
comes between scheduled and published
cards.use: see a post that is being sent right now
not: shows that it was approved

cards.subject: The published status
says: shows that the post is live
is the end of the normal flow
cards.use: see a post that has gone out successfully
not: shows that it is waiting to be scheduled

cards.subject: The partially-published status
says: shows that some channels published and at least one did not
is the outcome when one channel fails and others succeed
cards.use: see a post that went out on two channels but not a third
not: means every channel published

cards.subject: The failed status
says: shows that a post could not be published
calls for you to check the channel and try again
cards.use: see a post that did not go out
not: means the post went out on every channel

cards.subject: A comment on a post
says: lets a reviewer explain what to fix
stays with the post for the team to read
cards.use: want to leave feedback without changing the text
not: publishes the post

cards.subject: A change request
says: sends the post back to its author
is how an approver asks for edits
cards.use: are an approver and want edits made
not: lets an approver edit the post

cards.subject: Per-channel statuses
says: track each channel of a post separately
explain why one post can be partly published
cards.use: want to know how a post can succeed on one channel and fail on another
not: are always identical across channels

cards.subject: The owner role
says: can do everything on a brand
is the only role that can archive the brand
cards.use: need to know who can archive a brand
not: can only read the brand

cards.subject: The admin role
says: manages channels, team and content
can add teammates to a brand
cards.use: need someone to connect channels and manage the team
not: can only comment on posts

cards.subject: The editor role
says: writes, schedules and publishes posts
cannot manage channels or the team
cards.use: need someone to write and schedule posts
not: can only review without editing

cards.subject: The approver role
says: reviews posts and can comment or request changes
cannot edit what they review
cards.use: need a sign-off step that does not change the content
not: can write and schedule posts

cards.subject: The viewer role
says: can read but not change anything
suits someone who only needs to watch progress
cards.use: need to give a stakeholder read-only access
not: can approve posts

cards.subject: Per-brand roles
says: mean one person can hold different roles in different brands
are set brand by brand
cards.use: work with several brands and need different access in each
not: apply to the whole account at once

cards.subject: Least privilege
says: gives each person only the access their job needs
reduces the damage a mistake or stolen login can do
cards.use: choose a role for a new teammate
not: gives everyone admin to save time

cards.subject: The role check on every action
says: is repeated each time an action is attempted
means hiding a button is not what protects the brand
cards.use: wonder whether a viewer could get around a hidden button
not: only happens when a person signs in

cards.subject: Inviting a teammate
says: is done by an admin or the owner
lets the person sign up and join the brand
cards.use: want a colleague to join a brand
not: can be done by any viewer

cards.subject: A must rule
says: stops a post from being scheduled or approved when broken
is stronger than a suggestion
cards.use: need a limit that cannot be bypassed
not: is only a gentle hint

cards.subject: Master instructions
says: describe how each format and kind of engagement should be done
are the standing guidance for the brand's content
cards.use: want to know how a format should be written
not: are limits on media size

cards.subject: The title-word limit
says: caps how many words a title may have
is checked by the app itself
cards.use: are writing a title for a platform that has titles
not: limits the number of hashtags

cards.subject: The hashtag-count limit
says: caps how many hashtags a post may carry
is checked by the app itself
cards.use: are tempted to add a dozen hashtags
not: limits title words

cards.subject: The copy-length limit
says: caps how long the body text may be
is checked before scheduling
cards.use: have a long caption
not: limits image shape

cards.subject: The aspect-ratio limit
says: checks the shape of an image or video
guards against awkward cropping
cards.use: upload media of an unusual shape
not: limits caption length

cards.subject: A format
says: is a kind of post that the Playbook can give its own instructions and limits
lets the rules differ between, for example, a short post and a video
cards.use: want to apply the right guidance to a kind of post
not: is a person's role on a brand

cards.subject: Engagement guidelines
says: cover how to reply to comments and messages
set the expected manner when talking with the audience
cards.use: want to know how to answer a comment
not: are limits on hashtag count

cards.subject: Reach
says: counts the distinct people who saw a post
is not the same as the number of views
cards.use: want to know how many different people saw a post
not: counts every time the post was shown

cards.subject: Impressions
says: count every time a post was shown
can exceed reach because one person may see a post twice
cards.use: want to know how often a post was displayed
not: count only different people

cards.subject: Engagement
says: counts actions such as likes, comments, shares and saves
shows that people did more than just see the post
cards.use: want to know whether people responded
not: counts people who scrolled past

cards.subject: Engagement rate
says: divides engagement by an audience measure
lets posts with different audience sizes be compared
cards.use: want to compare a small account's post with a large one
not: is the raw number of likes

cards.subject: Click-through rate
says: divides link clicks by the number of times the post was seen
shows how persuasive the link was
cards.use: want to judge how well a link in a post worked
not: divides comments by followers

cards.subject: Follower growth
says: tracks how the audience size changes over time
is best read next to what you posted
cards.use: want to know if the audience is growing
not: counts likes on a single post

cards.subject: A vanity metric
says: looks impressive without telling you what to do next
can rise while the business goal stays flat
cards.use: are tempted to celebrate a big number that changes nothing
not: is always the most useful number

cards.subject: Benchmarking against yourself
says: compares new results with your own past results
is usually fairer than comparing with a different account
cards.use: want to know if a post did well for you
not: compares you only with the largest accounts

cards.subject: Metrics that vary by platform
says: mean the numbers GGSocial shows depend on what each platform returns
can differ in name and meaning between platforms
cards.use: find that two platforms report different measures
not: are identical on every platform

cards.subject: A UTM parameter
says: tags a link so visits can be traced to a post
shows up in a website's own analytics
cards.use: want to see in your site analytics which post sent a visitor
not: changes the picture size

cards.subject: A reporting period
says: is the span of time that a report covers
should match the length of a campaign for a fair read
cards.use: want to compare this month with last
not: is the time of day a post goes out

cards.subject: A sample size
says: is how many posts a conclusion rests on
makes a result from one post unreliable
cards.use: are about to change strategy after one post did well
not: is the number of followers

cards.subject: Attribution
says: is deciding which post or action gets credit for a result
is rarely exact because people see many things before acting
cards.use: are asked which single post caused a sale
not: is a metric every platform reports

cards.subject: A strong password
says: is long and unique to one service
is not a word or a pattern easy to guess
cards.use: are choosing a password for GGSocial
not: is your name followed by a number

cards.subject: Password reuse
says: lets one breach unlock several accounts
is why a different password is needed per service
cards.use: are tempted to use your email password everywhere
not: is safe if the password is long

cards.subject: A password manager
says: stores a different strong password for each service
fills passwords only on the right site
cards.use: cannot remember a unique password for every service
not: sends your passwords to your teammates

cards.subject: Two-step verification
says: asks for a second proof besides the password
protects an account even if the password leaks
cards.use: want an account to survive a stolen password
not: replaces the password completely

cards.subject: Phishing
says: tricks you into giving a password through a fake page or message
often imitates a platform or a colleague
cards.use: get an email asking you to sign in through a link
not: is a safe way to reset a password

cards.subject: A fake verification message
says: claims your account will be closed unless you act
aims to steal a login or a code
cards.use: get a direct message warning of an urgent account closure
not: is sent by GGSocial to prove you are genuine

cards.subject: Removing a departed teammate
says: takes away access when someone leaves
is done by an admin or the owner
cards.use: have a colleague who no longer works on the brand
not: can wait until their password changes

cards.subject: Never sharing a password in chat
says: keeps a password out of messages that can be forwarded
is replaced by inviting people with their own login
cards.use: need a colleague to get access
not: is fine when you trust the person

cards.subject: Reviewing connected apps
says: lists the apps allowed to act on your platform account
lets you remove ones you no longer use
cards.use: want to cut down on old access to your accounts
not: happens automatically every day

cards.subject: A shared computer
says: is a risk if you stay signed in
calls for signing out when you finish
cards.use: are signing in on a machine other people use
not: is fine if you close the tab

cards.subject: An unexpected sign-in alert
says: calls for changing the password and checking connected channels
should be treated as possible unauthorised access
cards.use: get a notice about a sign-in that was not you
not: can be ignored

cards.subject: Replying promptly
says: shows the audience that someone is listening
builds trust over time
cards.use: have comments waiting on a post
not: is optional and has no effect on trust

cards.subject: Sponsored disclosure
says: tells the audience that a post is paid or gifted
is expected by platforms and regulators
cards.use: post something a partner paid for
not: is optional if the audience can guess

cards.subject: Reddit self-promotion
says: is limited by many communities' own rules
goes down better when the post offers value first
cards.use: want to share your product on Reddit
not: is welcome in every subreddit
like: The Reddit title and subreddit rule

cards.subject: Buying followers
says: adds accounts that do not engage
can hurt a platform's trust in the account
cards.use: are tempted to inflate your follower count
not: raises genuine engagement

cards.subject: Permission for images
says: is needed when a picture belongs to someone else
avoids copyright complaints
cards.use: want to use a photo you found online
not: is not needed if you credit the site

cards.subject: Handling a negative comment
says: answers calmly and offers to help
moves a complex complaint to a private channel
cards.use: get an angry public comment
not: deletes it quickly to hide it

cards.subject: Posting identical text everywhere
says: can look like spam on platforms that value native content
is avoided by tuning a post for each channel
cards.use: are about to paste the same copy on every platform
not: is the best way to save time

cards.subject: Pausing during a sensitive event
says: holds scheduled posts when the world is mourning or in crisis
avoids a cheerful promotion landing at a bad moment
cards.use: see major bad news just before posts are due
not: means keeping the schedule unchanged

cards.subject: Tagging and mentioning
says: notifies the person or brand you name
should be used only when it is relevant to them
cards.use: want to credit a partner in a post
not: is harmless however often you do it

cards.subject: Respecting privacy
says: avoids posting personal details about customers
needs consent before a customer is featured
cards.use: want to share a customer's message
not: is unnecessary if the message was public

cards.subject: The content strategist agent
says: keeps the content plan ahead of the calendar
works at the level of ideas
cards.use: want a plan of topics before posts are written
not: drafts replies to comments

cards.subject: The content writer agent
says: keeps the calendar full from the plan
books posts into open slots and revises work sent back
cards.use: want posts written from the plan and placed on the calendar
not: reports on yesterday's results

cards.subject: The community manager agent
says: drafts replies to comments, messages, mentions and reviews
flags anything a person must decide
cards.use: want help answering your audience
not: writes the weekly performance report

cards.subject: The performance analyst agent
says: reads yesterday's posts each morning
writes weekly and monthly reports
cards.use: want a regular summary of how posts performed
not: answers customers

cards.subject: Review on every step
says: is on until the brand owner switches it off
means a person checks agent work before it moves on
cards.use: switch agents on for the first time
not: is off by default

cards.subject: The reviewer score
says: rates agent output out of 100
flags risks as well as quality
cards.use: want to know how agent work is judged
not: is set by the audience

cards.subject: Weak but safe work
says: goes back to the agent once with fixes
does not need a person yet
cards.use: see agent output with a low score and no risk
not: is published straight away

cards.subject: A safety stop
says: pauses a run whatever the review setting
protects against risky content going out
cards.use: want to know what always needs a person
not: can be switched off for convenience

cards.subject: Risky topics such as prices and refunds
says: always stop for a person
include legal and health matters too
cards.use: have an agent draft a reply about money back
not: are handled by the agent alone

cards.subject: The daily AI budget
says: is a limit on what the agents may spend in a day
pauses a run for a person once it is spent
cards.use: want to know why agent work stopped partway
not: has no effect on agent runs

qa.q: What is a channel in GGSocial?
qa.right: One account on one platform, owned by one brand
qa.why: A channel is a single account on a single platform.

qa.q: What is the length limit for a standard post on X in the Composer?
qa.right: 280 characters
qa.why: X caps at 280 characters and the Composer counts live.

qa.q: Which platform needs media on every post?
qa.right: Instagram
qa.why: Instagram needs an image or video.

qa.q: What does a Reddit post need?
qa.right: A title and a subreddit
qa.why: Reddit needs a title and a subreddit.

qa.q: How do people sign in to GGSocial?
qa.right: With an email address and a password
qa.why: Accounts use email and password.

qa.q: Where do you write one piece of copy for several channels?
qa.right: The Composer
qa.why: The Composer holds base copy and overrides.

qa.q: What is the difference between a live and a manual-only channel?
qa.right: A live channel is published to by GGSocial; a manual-only channel ends with a person posting
qa.why: Manual-only platforms offer no write API for organic content.

qa.q: In what order does a post normally move through approval?
qa.right: Draft, needs approval, approved, scheduled
qa.why: A post is approved before it is scheduled.

qa.q: Which role can review posts but cannot edit them?
qa.right: Approver
qa.why: An approver reviews only.

qa.q: Which role is read-only?
qa.right: Viewer
qa.why: A viewer can look but not change.

qa.q: Where do you finish a post for a manual-only channel?
qa.right: In the Publish queue
qa.why: The queue holds copy buttons, media and steps.

qa.q: Are roles global for the whole account or per brand?
qa.right: Per brand
qa.why: A person can hold different roles in different brands.

qa.q: What does a Playbook rule marked as must do?
qa.right: Scheduling and approval refuse a post that breaks it
qa.why: Must rules block scheduling and approval.

qa.q: In which timezone is a post's scheduled time shown?
qa.right: The brand's own timezone
qa.why: The time is an absolute instant shown in the brand's timezone.

qa.q: You have posted a queued item by hand. What do you do in GGSocial?
qa.right: Tick it off in the queue so it is marked published
qa.why: Ticking the item off marks it published.

qa.q: Which role is the minimum needed to schedule and publish posts?
qa.right: Editor
qa.why: Editing and publishing need editor or above.

qa.q: Which role can connect channels and manage the team?
qa.right: Admin or above
qa.why: Managing channels and team needs admin or above.

qa.q: Only one role can archive a brand. Which?
qa.right: Owner
qa.why: Archiving is reserved for the owner.

qa.q: What is the best way to tune wording for one platform only?
qa.right: Override the base copy on that channel
qa.why: A channel override leaves other channels alone.

qa.q: Which view shows every brand on a single month grid?
qa.right: The Calendar
qa.why: The Calendar is colour-coded by brand.

qa.q: A draft for X is 400 characters. What can you do?
qa.right: Shorten it or split it into a thread with blank lines
qa.why: X caps at 280 and can thread on blank lines.

qa.q: You are an approver and spot a typo. What is the right move?
qa.right: Comment or request changes so an editor fixes it
wrong: Ask a viewer to fix it
qa.why: Approvers cannot edit.

qa.q: A post is published on two channels but fails on a third. Which overall status fits?
qa.right: Partially published
qa.why: Each channel has its own status.

qa.q: A viewer opens a direct link to an edit action. What happens?
qa.right: GGSocial checks their role again and refuses
qa.why: Hiding a button is not the security boundary.

qa.q: A post to a channel fails and the channel shows expired. What is the best first step?
qa.right: Reconnect the channel through the platform's sign-in
qa.why: Expired access is restored by reconnecting.

qa.q: A colleague leaves the team. What should an admin do?
qa.right: Remove their access to the brand
wrong: Wait for their password to change
Make them a viewer for ever
qa.why: Departed teammates should lose access promptly.

qa.q: A teammate asks for your password so they can post. What should you do?
qa.right: Invite them so they have their own login
qa.why: Never share passwords; invite people instead.

qa.q: An email says your account will close unless you sign in through a link. What should you do?
qa.right: Ignore the link and go to the site directly
qa.why: This is typical phishing.

qa.q: Which is the strongest way to protect a login?
qa.right: A unique long password plus two-step verification
wrong: The same password as your email
A password shared with the team
qa.why: Unique password and a second step.

qa.q: A manual-only post is due but you cannot post it yet. What should you not do?
qa.right: Tick it off as published
wrong: Ask a teammate to take over
qa.why: Ticking off tells GGSocial it is live.

qa.q: An agent drafts a reply promising a refund. What happens?
qa.right: The run pauses for a person
qa.why: Prices, refunds, legal and health matters always stop for a person.

qa.q: Which agent reads yesterday's posts each morning?
qa.right: The performance analyst
qa.why: The analyst turns results into reports.

qa.q: Where does everything waiting for a person land?
qa.right: The Review inbox
qa.why: You can approve, send back with a note or stop the run.

qa.q: Who can switch off review for a brand's agent steps?
qa.right: The brand owner
qa.why: The reason is kept in the log.

qa.q: Agent work scores weak but is safe. What happens?
qa.right: It goes back to the agent once with fixes
qa.why: Weak but safe work gets one chance to improve.

qa.q: What is logged for every AI call GGSocial makes?
qa.right: Its cost
qa.why: AI usage and cost are logged.

qa.q: You see a post with a large reach but almost no clicks on its link. What should you check first?
qa.right: Whether the call to action and link placement were clear
wrong: Whether the Calendar colour was right
qa.why: Reach without clicks points at the call to action.

qa.q: A small account's post got 50 likes and a big account's got 500. Which comparison is fairer?
qa.right: Engagement rate
qa.why: Rates adjust for audience size.

qa.q: Your audience is in several countries. What is a sensible approach?
qa.right: Post at more than one hour and learn from analytics
wrong: Pick the most popular hour for one country
qa.why: No single hour suits everyone.

qa.q: You want to know which post sent visitors to your site. What helps?
qa.right: Tag the link with a UTM parameter
qa.why: UTM tags show up in site analytics.

qa.q: A public comment is angry and rude. What is a good response?
qa.right: Reply calmly and offer to continue in private
qa.why: Calm replies build trust.

qa.q: You want to use a photo from a website. What should you do first?
qa.right: Get permission from the owner
wrong: Use it, as it is public
qa.why: Credit does not replace permission.

qa.q: A partner paid you to post about their product. What should the post include?
qa.right: A clear note that it is sponsored
qa.why: Disclosure is expected.

qa.q: Major bad news breaks just before a cheerful promotion is due. What should you do?
qa.right: Pause or reschedule the post
wrong: Reply to every comment at once
qa.why: Check the mood before promotion goes out.

qa.q: You paste the same text on X, Instagram and Reddit. What is the main risk?
qa.right: It can read as spam and miss each platform's norms
qa.why: Tune a post for each channel.

qa.q: You are about to contact support about a failed post. What should you include?
qa.right: Brand, channel, what you expected, what happened and the exact error
qa.why: Specific reports are solved faster.

qa.q: Support asks for your password to look into the problem. What should you do?
qa.right: Decline and offer other details
qa.why: A genuine team never needs it.

qa.q: A channel has errored and three posts are scheduled to it. What is the best step?
qa.right: Look at the channel, fix it, then check the scheduled posts
qa.why: Fix the cause before more posts pile up.

qa.q: You post a lot of selling and engagement drops. What does this suggest?
qa.right: The content mix needs more helpful or entertaining posts
qa.why: A feed of only promotion tires an audience.

qa.q: You need a sign-off step without letting the reviewer change the text. Which role?
qa.right: Approver
qa.why: Approvers cannot edit.

qa.q: Post copy fits in the Composer but is rejected by the platform. What could explain it?
qa.right: Emoji or the platform's rules counting differently
qa.why: Platforms count characters their own way and change rules.

qa.q: One post changed hands from author to approver, who asked for edits. What status does it show?
qa.right: Changes requested
qa.why: A change request returns the post to its author.

qa.q: Why might a platform be manual-only?
qa.right: It offers no write API for organic posts
qa.why: Some platforms offer no way to publish automatically.

qa.q: A result looked great on a single post. Why is it risky to rewrite the whole strategy?
qa.right: One post is a tiny sample
qa.why: One result can be luck.
